/ai-form-builder/job-application-form.note: craft: Two classes. (1) Tacked-on sentence: faq item 6 ends 'Others call it an employment application form.' It is appended after 'Some employers print that title at the top of the page, but the questions underneath and the signed certification do not change.', so 'Others' points back across a sentence about something else; it exists to place a secondary. Fix: fold the name into the opening ('Yes. Application for employment form and employment application form are longer names for the same document.') and end on the certification point. Only instance. (2) Serial comma used inconsistently (HUB_RULES 2a 'Consistent'). With the comma: feature_1 'a date picker for the start date, a phone field, and a block that repeats'; feature_5 'role, location, stage, and owner'; howto_step_1 'the right to work, and pay expectations'; faq item 3 'education, references, and a signed, dated certification'. Without: why_description 'The form, the applicant table and the manager alerts'; tab_image_1 alt 'a store, a start date and the shifts the applicant can work'. Pick one style and apply it to all six. | voice: (1) All four tab H3s use one formula, '[article] [modifier] application that [verb phrase]': tab_content_1 'An hourly job application that leads with availability'; tab_content_2 'A clinical job application that checks every credential'; tab_content_3 'An internal application that loops in the manager'; tab_content_4 'A professional application that sorts by must-haves'. Four in a row is the machine rhythm HUB_RULES 2b names, and HUB_RULES 5 says the tab H3 names the outcome, not the form type. Pages rewritten today do this (sales-automation 'Catch quiet deals before the forecast call'; AP 'Route each entity's bills to its own controller'). Fix: four outcome headings with different shapes, e.g. 'See who can cover weekends before you call', 'Catch a lapsing license before the interview'. (2) Three FAQ answers in a row open the same way: faq item 4 'Yes. Your form can produce...', item 5 'Yes. Ask Emergent for...', item 6 'Yes. An application for employment form is...'. Vary at least one (item 6 can open 'They are the same document.'). (3) Vague phrasing where a specific word belongs: hero_description 'every answer stays in data you own' (an answer stays in a database, not in 'data'); features_subheading 'These six pieces turn the answers into a shortlist' ('pieces' is filler, and feature_4 (PDF copies) and feature_6 (source code) have nothing to do with a shortlist). Fix: name what the six features cover, e.g. 'Below: the sections, the role branching, the uploads, the PDFs, the applicant table and where the form lives.' | truth: (1) The must-have rule in tab_content_4 is unclear and does not match the image: the copy says applicants 'answer the must-have questions: work authorization and salary range. Missing either one sends the application to a hold list.' A required question cannot be 'missing', and the copy never says what makes a salary range pass. The image's rule is a value test: 'Authorized, salary in range' / 'Salary in range, not authorized'. The mockup officeAndRemote has the same gap ('two must-have questions: work authorization and salary range. Put anyone who misses a must-have on a hold list'). Fix: state the rule in copy and mockup, e.g. 'Anyone without work authorization, or asking above the posted band, goes to a hold list.' (2) Heading overclaims: tab_content_2 H3 'checks every credential'. The body only collects a license number, issuing state and expiry and flags expiry within 60 days. Nothing is verified, and the CMA row has no check at all. Fix: say what happens ('flags a license before it lapses'). Earlier fixes verified: why_description no longer generalizes about competitors; CMA is now 'medical assistants give their certification'; tenure is checked before submit in copy and image; feature_5 says 'never caps applications'; FAQ 4 answers the blank PDF first; FAQ 9 is about roles.
